prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you ate a salad at a barbecue. Respond to the committee.
response:
*adjusts microphone, clears throat*

Mr. Chairman, members of the committee, I appear before you today under protest, but with a clean conscience.

The allegations before this body—that I consumed salad at a barbecue—are baseless fabrications, likely spread by elements hostile to the traditional cookout way of life. I ask you: who stands to gain from such slander? The potato salad industrial complex? The coleslaw lobby?

I will not dignify these accusations by invoking my Fifth Amendment rights, for I have nothing to hide. I am prepared to answer fully.

On the date in question, I consumed the following: one cheeseburger, medium-rare; a bratwurst; baked beans; potato chips; and a slice of apple pie. My beverage was a domestic beer. I had *coleslaw*—which this committee knows full well is a condiment, not a salad in any meaningful ideological sense.

I categorically deny the charge of salad-eating. I have never been a member of the Arugula Party. I have never attended a meeting of the Kale Front. My loyalty to the grill is unwavering.

I am prepared to name names, Mr. Chairman. I saw Representative Wilson eating a *veggie burger*. I have documents.

*leans back*

I yield the remainder of my time.
